risks: The protocol changes the timing of a routine step; the main risk is re-escalation or deterioration after stopping, mitigated by the age limit, restart criteria, PICU review of every re-escalation and a stopping rule.
consent: Screened as quality improvement; parents receive the criteria card and are told the ward is using a new weaning protocol; they can ask for stepwise weaning and the attending may decline a trial off for clinical reasons.
data: The bedside log records bed, date, times and restarts; the run chart holds no names; charts are read by ward staff with routine access.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: families with limited English, low health literacy or who live far from the hospital may understand less or return elsewhere; the criteria card is translated into the two most common languages and the 7-day call uses interpreters.
effectiveness: Success is a sustained shift in time on high flow for infants aged 8 weeks or older without breaching the safety stopping rule.
efficiency: Uses existing staff and chart data; about a minute per check for the log.
costs: Printing of criteria cards; staff time within normal shifts.
grants: None needed; a multi-site study of infants under 8 weeks would need external funding.
partnerships: PICU lead, respiratory therapy supervisor, night nurse representatives and two parents from the family advisory council.
rebPath: Screened as quality improvement by the pediatric quality committee (QC-PED-2026-044); publication will follow SQUIRE 2.0 and the journal's QI policy.
limitations: Single ward, one season, historical baseline; the young-infant question is not answered.
summary: QI with an age limit, a safety stopping rule and translated criteria cards for families.
